output:
I'll start by reading the docs and the package layout.

The last shell call was malformed and didn't run. I'm applying the fixes now.

I'll use the edit tool instead, one file at a time, starting with `parse.py`.

Some of the parallel edits failed with I/O errors. I'll check which ones actually landed.

Two edits were lost, the `candidates` sort key and the `moved` count. I'll redo them one at a time.

The unit tests pass now. Next I'll run the check tool and look at output encoding and the remaining edge cases.

I'll check that each of the 8 refused cases is a legitimate error.

All 8 refusals match the doc rules. I'll make one small hardening change so the header regex matches only ASCII digits, then write the status file.

I fixed the `patchkit` bugs under `/app/patchkit`, and all 46 unit tests now pass (`python -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`). `tools/check.py --data data` reports 0 broken on all 142 applied cases. It can't tell whether a hunk landed in the right place, so I also read the code against the docs. I wrote `/app/STATUS.json` with status `success`.

I read `docs/apply.md` and `docs/changelog.md` as authoritative. `overview.md` 3.4 describes the old nearest-match order, which the archive marks as withdrawn.

The changes, by file:
- **`parse.py`:**
  - The carriage return before each line feed is stripped from every patch line.
  - Header paths end at the first tab, not at any whitespace.
  - A range with no count now has a count of 1.
  - Reversing a patch swaps the end-of-file markers along with their lines.
  - The hunk-header regex matches ASCII digits only.
- **`apply.py`:**
  - A hunk with an empty old range is expected right after line `A`.
  - Added lines take the file's line ending instead of always LF.
  - Offsets are measured from the stated line, not from the carried position.
  - A hunk can no longer apply before the end of the previous applied hunk.
- **`search.py`:**
  - Fuzz levels are tried one after another, each over every candidate position.
  - At equal distance, the lower line number is tried first.
- **`report.py`:**
  - Result entries stay in patch order instead of being sorted by path.
  - `moved` counts only hunks with a non-zero offset.

I checked the 8 cases the package now refuses against the docs, by reading the error each one raises. A few I also read in full. I did not check them one by one beyond that. An all-context hunk at non-zero fuzz is a corner the docs leave ambiguous, and I didn't change how it's handled.

command_result.command: cd /app && find . -path ./.git -prune -o -type f -print | head -100 && cat docs/overview.md && wc -l docs/* patchkit/*.py tests/*.py
cd /app && cat docs/cases.md docs/patch.md docs/paths.md docs/lines.md docs/apply.md docs/output.md docs/changelog.md; ls docs/archive tools data | head -30
cd /app && cat docs/lines.md; head -12 docs/apply.md; sed -n 25,40p patchkit/lines.py; cat patchkit/parse.py | head -100
cd /app && cat docs/lines.md; head -12 docs/apply.md; sed -n 25,40p patchkit/lines.py
cd /app && sed -n 100,112p patchkit/parse.py; python -m unittest discover -s tests -t . 2>&1 | tail -60; cat tests/support.py; ls tests/expected | head; cat docs/archive/*

cd /app && git diff 2>/dev/null | head -5; grep -n 'new_eol, hl.old_eol\|offset\|fuzz\|>0' patchkit/parse.py patchkit/report.py | head -20; cat patchkit/search.py | sed -n 18,30p; sed -n 40,65p patchkit/search.py; cat patchkit/apply.py | sed -n 8,50p

cd /app && sed -i 's/(abs(p - expected), -p)/(abs(p - expected), p)/' patchkit/search.py && sed -i 's/h\["offset"\] != 0 or h\["fuzz"\] > 0 for/h["offset"] != 0 for/' patchkit/report.py && grep -n 'abs(p' patchkit/search.py; grep -n moved patchkit/report.py; python -m unittest discover -s tests -t . 2>&1 | tail -30; ls tools; python tools/check.py data 2>&1 | tail -20

cd /app && python tools/check.py --data data 2>&1 | tail -20; grep -lP '[^\x00-\x7f]' tests/expected/results/* data/cases/* | head; grep -l 'u00' tests/expected/results/* | head -3; ls data/cases | wc -l; python -m patchkit run --out /tmp/o && cat /tmp/o/errors.json | head -30

cd /app && tail -8 /tmp/o/errors.json; for c in 036 082 117 120; do echo == $c; python - <<EOF
import json
d=json.load(open('data/cases/case-$c.json'))
print(d.get('options'));print(d['patch'][:1800])
EOF
done

cd /app && sed -i 's/@@(?: |\$)")/@@(?: |$)", re.ASCII)/' patchkit/parse.py && grep -n 'HEADER =' patchkit/parse.py && python -m unittest discover -s tests -t . 2>&1 | tail -3 && cat > STATUS.json <<'EOF'
{"status": "success", "summary": "Fixed patchkit per the docs: CR stripping and tab-only path ends in patch parsing, default range count 1, reverse swapping end-of-file markers, empty-range expected position, file-ending for added lines, fuzz levels tried in turn, lower-first tie order, no overlap/reordering of hunks, offsets from the stated line, patch-order file entries and the moved count. Unit tests and tools/check.py pass."}
EOF
cat STATUS.json
